value.title: Cited-premise Theorem 9 private-message converse foundations
value.summary: Develop the private-message specialization, auxiliary-receiver marginalization, and restricted-posterior foundations that follow conditionally from the explicitly encoded Gohari--Liu--Nair Theorem 9 premise, without asserting source fidelity, authenticating that premise, or claiming a numerical capacity bound.

value.title: Conditional Theorem 9 private-message specialization and input-only receiver reduction
value.summary:
Accepted statement (exact): Assume the cited Gohari--Liu--Nair Theorem 9 outer-bound premise exactly as encoded in theorem9_spec.json and displayed for review in SOURCE_TRANSCRIPTION.md: for every finite auxiliary-receiver law T_{G,K|X,Y,Z}, achievable rates obey the stated factorization, equations (19a)-(19p), and both side conditions. Then setting R0=0 and exhaustively expanding the displayed minima and interval conditions gives exactly the independently generated local 30-row system; the exhaustive single-output term audit proves that replacing G,K by their input-only product marginals preserves the entire system, and hence for the physical BSSC C_sum <= inf_{finite-output binary-input T_{G|X},T_{K|X}} B(G,K). With the explicit extended-real local definitions (including sup(empty set)=-infinity), V_Q(G,K) <= V(1/2;G,K) <= B(G,K), and every Q0-supported row depends on the receiver channels only through (c,g,k,c), making V_0(g,k) finite and well defined on its realizable (g,k)-domain. No PDF-origin, source-fidelity, rendering, or visual-semantic assertion is part of this claim.

Scope qualifications (exact): Validity is conditional on the factorization, equations (19a)-(19p), side conditions, and quantifier order encoded in theorem9_spec.json and displayed in SOURCE_TRANSCRIPTION.md. The record does not establish fidelity to the cited PDF, correctness of the original Gohari–Liu–Nair theorem, or any PDF-origin, rendering, or visual-semantic assertion. The converse infimum ranges over finite-output, binary-input input-only channels T_{G|X} and T_{K|X}. V_0(g,k) is asserted to be well defined and finite only on the realizable (g,k)-domain. No additional authenticated-source, numerical-bound, cardinality, or continuum-optimization assertion is established.

value.title: Proof of the conditional 30-row specialization, marginalization, and restricted-value consequences
value.summary: Starting from the explicitly assumed encoded Theorem 9 premise, set R0=0, expand the displayed minima into 26 scalar rows, and split the two interval side conditions into four nonnegative-slack rows. Exact comparison with the independently generated local path rows establishes the stated 30-row specialization. The exhaustive output-term audit shows that every information term contains only one auxiliary group and one receiver output; consequently, replacing an admitted joint auxiliary-receiver law by the product of its input-only G and K marginals preserves each required marginal and every row. The premise's quantifier order then gives the stated infimum bound without interchanging the receiver infimum and input-prior supremum. Restricted feasible-set inclusion gives V_Q(G,K) <= V(1/2;G,K) <= B(G,K). For Q0-supported hierarchies, the endpoint receiver-information functions vanish, so the posterior identities reduce every audited row to the four midpoint values (c,g,k,c). The explicit zero-rate hierarchy and binary-output individual-rate bounds establish the claimed finiteness on the realizable (g,k)-domain.

value.title: Structured-premise row expansion and exhaustive single-output term audit
value.summary: The accepted claim is established using two exact constructions of the private-message constraint system: direct expansion of the structured equations (19a)-(19p) and side conditions, and independent generation from generic three-link path formulas. Rows are compared after only the chain-rule normalizations I(U,W;A)=I(W;A)+I(U;A|W) and I(V,W;A)=I(W;A)+I(V;A|W). A separately encoded exhaustive whitelist records every output-bearing term and verifies the absence of joint-(G,K) output terms or conditioning of one output on another. This method is used only for the accepted conditional specialization and input-only marginalization result; it does not authenticate the cited premise or optimize the resulting converse.

value.title: Exact verifier for the encoded Theorem 9 private-message specialization
value.summary: The standard-library Python verifier reads theorem9_spec.json as the explicit mathematical premise, checks its factorization, all 16 equation labels, and both side conditions, expands the premise to 30 rows, independently constructs the corresponding three-link path rows, and compares rate coefficients and signed information terms exactly. It also checks the separately encoded 3/12/12/3 single-output term audit. The verifier uses exact integer linear forms and makes no PDF, network, rendering, optimizer, or source-authentication assertion.
